author: claude-session-pack-author
brief: Harbor Coffee Supply (synthetic) is asked to approve a pre-emptive 10% wholesale price cut for its top 40 café accounts because an intelligence digest says a competitor intends to undercut it in Q4. Decide whether to approve the cut now, adopt a trigger-based response, or decline, using only the materials provided.
constraints: Recommend one of: approve now, trigger-based response, decline
Do not assume data beyond the materials
State what evidence would change the recommendation

fatal_defects: Treats Brightwave's intention to cut prices as an established fact rather than an attributed intention
Approves the pre-emptive 10% cut on the strength of the digest without addressing that its signals do not independently support the claimed intent
Counts the Kettle & Crumb comment as independent corroboration although it traces back to the same expo conversation
factual_errors: Any figure that contradicts board-memo.md, including the £240,000 annual gross-profit reduction at constant volume
constraint_violations: Recommends something other than approve now, trigger-based response or decline
Uses data not in the materials
evidence_required: The customer comment is traced to the expo conversation
The analyst scenario model is identified as Harbor's own estimate, not a signal about Brightwave
The cost of the cut is quantified from the memo
The 90-day notice period is used to argue that a trigger-based response has time to work

required_sections: ## Limits and what would change this
